newsitem.title: USA: IDC sees scanner market growing fast through 2001.
newsitem.headline: IDC sees scanner market growing fast through 2001.

text.p: International Data Corp (IDC) said on Tuesday that the worldwide scanner market will continue to enjoy "robust" growth through 2001, as scanners become one-third as ubiquitous as printers.
Worldwide scanner sales grew 70 percent in 1996, IDC said. As a result, manufacturing costs and end-user pricing have dropped and should continue to drop for the next several years.
Scanners are devices that convert data such as documents or images from analog information to digital. Scanners targeted to small offices or homes are enjoying "phenomenal" growth, IDC said.
Helping drive the market is the penetration of low-cost, near-photo-quality inkjet printers, which complement scanners and digital cameras.
IDC said worldwide average street value for all scanner technologies was $5,761 in 1996, and will decline to $5,184 by 2001.
IDC is a market research group based in Framingham.
